# Ryva Master GTM Plan (Second-Run Focus)

Date: 2026-04-03
Owner: Ege
Window: Next 30 days

## Objective

Turn first-run curiosity into second-run habit, then paid dependency.

## Core Thesis

- First run = interesting.
- Second run = behavior change.
- Third run = dependency.
- No second run = no GTM progress, even with high reply volume.

## What We Optimize For

- Depth over breadth.
- 3 active teams at a time (`CyberMinds + 2`).
- Delta updates over full summaries.
- Urgency and risk, not just correctness.

## Non-Negotiables (Every Run Message)

1. Reference last run.
2. Show what changed vs what is still unresolved.
3. Tie unresolved item to concrete risk/cost.
4. Ask one forced binary question.
5. Time-anchor next run ("after next merge cycle", "before standup", "EOD").

If a message misses any of the 5, it does not ship.

## Offer Structure

- Do not sell on first run.
- Ask for continuation, not commitment:
 - "Want me to run this again after your next merge cycle?"
- Payment ask only after run #2 or #3:
 - "If this replaced standup reconstruction this week, would you pay for it?"

## Daily Execution (Simple)

1. Active-team block (first 2 hours)

- Send second-run delta updates to all 3 active teams.
- Include 1 forced binary question per team.
- Lock next-run timing in-thread for responders.

2. Warm-responder conversion block

- Send first-run artifact to 5 warm responders (not cold leads).
- Use their exact pain wording.
- End with one forced question.

3. Outreach block (top-of-funnel maintenance)

- 10 targeted X replies/DMs.
- 10 targeted Reddit replies/DMs.
- Insight-first, no feature pitch.

4. Proof distribution block

- Publish 1 short proof post (X/LinkedIn/Reddit rotation).
- Show one real missed decision + one "do this now" action.

## Message Templates

### First Run (Warm Responder)

`text
You mentioned [pain]. Pulled a pass from your last 24h:
- Decisions made: [x]
- Missing decision: [y]
- Next action: [z]

Is [y] actually decided or still open?
`

### Second Run (Delta)

`text
Since last run:
- Changed: [x]
- Still unresolved: [y]
- New risk: [z impact]

Is [y] still blocked or resolved?
I will rerun this after your next merge cycle and send what changed.
`

### Payment Trigger (After Habit Signal)

`text
This is the third cycle where we caught decision drift before it became rework.
If this replaced standup reconstruction this week, would you pay for it?
`

## Qualification and Drop Rules

- Keep only teams with:
 - explicit standup/context pain
 - active project motion
 - at least one real reply
- Drop when:
 - no response after 2 high-quality run attempts
 - generic interest but no workflow engagement

## Metrics That Matter (Daily)

- Runs sent
- Second runs completed
- Follow-ups scheduled
- Meaningful replies
- Teams with weekly cadence
- Payment conversations started

Ignore vanity metrics (views, likes, impressions) for decision-making.

## 30-Day Targets

- 20-30 meaningful conversations
- 10+ repo runs
- 5+ second-run loops completed
- 3-5 teams using weekly
- 1-2 payment conversations

## Weekly Review (30 min)

- Which messages created second runs?
- Which risk framings triggered replies?
- Which teams are approaching dependency?
- Which threads should be killed?

## Start Today (No Warm-Up)

1. Select 2 teams besides CyberMinds.
2. Send 3 second-run delta messages in the first 2 hours.
3. Get 2 next-run timings confirmed in-thread.
4. Drop low-signal threads immediately.

This plan wins only if run cadence is enforced daily.

# Three.js Website Playbook

This playbook is based on the current state of this repo:

- `Next.js 16` App Router
- `TypeScript` with `strict: true`
- `@react-three/fiber`, `@react-three/drei`, `gsap`
- current app is a single-scene spike in `app/page.tsx` + `app/box.tsx`

This is a good starting point for learning cinematic 3D marketing sites.
It is not yet a production-ready workflow.

## Goal

Build interactive landing pages in the style of `igloo.inc`:

- strong visual composition
- 3D hero scene
- layered HTML typography
- subtle camera motion
- atmospheric lighting and fog
- performant enough to ship

## Time Estimate

Because you are already a full-stack dev, your timeline is shorter than a beginner's.

### Fastest realistic path

- `6-10 hours`: first credible 3D hero in this repo
- `20-40 hours`: one polished landing page you would actually show people
- `60-120 hours`: enough repetition to build these without guessing

### Practical timeline

- `Week 1`: understand the stack and build one proper hero scene
- `Week 2`: add imported assets, overlay UI, postprocessing, and motion
- `Week 3`: rebuild the hero from scratch with better taste and performance
- `Week 4+`: scroll-driven storytelling, custom materials, shader work, mobile tuning

If you work consistently:

- `1 weekend`: solid prototype
- `2-4 weeks`: strong portfolio-grade landing page
- `1-3 months`: real confidence with this class of websites

## Current Repo Assessment

What is already good:

- minimal project
- correct stack choice
- strict TypeScript
- direct iteration loop
- you already have R3F and GSAP installed

What is missing:

- scene architecture
- reusable components
- imported asset pipeline
- postprocessing
- typography layer
- performance constraints
- production scene composition

Current bottleneck:

You are still learning through primitives. That is useful for 1-2 sessions, but the next step is not "more cubes". The next step is one real hero section with a real asset.

## Core Rule

Do not learn Three.js as an abstract API first.

Learn it through one repeated product pattern:

1. full-screen hero
2. one focal 3D object
3. overlay text
4. subtle interaction
5. atmospheric lighting
6. performance budget

That is the shortest path to the kind of work you want.

## Build Order

Follow this exact order.

### Phase 1: Scene Architecture

Time: `1-2 hours`

Refactor the current single-file spike into a real structure.

Create:

- `components/scene/hero-scene.tsx`
- `components/scene/camera-rig.tsx`
- `components/scene/hero-model.tsx`
- `components/ui/hero-overlay.tsx`

Keep:

- `app/page.tsx` as composition only
- `app/layout.tsx` as app shell

Target result:

- page is readable
- scene logic is separated from UI logic
- camera logic is not mixed into model code

### Phase 2: Replace the Cube

Time: `2-4 hours`

Stop using a primitive as the main subject.

Create:

- `public/models/`
- add one `.glb` asset

Use:

- `useGLTF`
- `preload`
- explicit scale and position

Target result:

- one imported 3D model centered in a controlled hero

Recommended first asset:

- one abstract sculpture
- one product-like object
- one stylized architectural form

Avoid:

- huge environment scenes
- detailed animated characters
- multi-hundred-MB files

### Phase 3: Light the Scene Correctly

Time: `2-3 hours`

Learn these first:

- `ambientLight`
- `directionalLight`
- `spotLight`
- `Environment`
- fog

Your goal is not "realistic lighting".
Your goal is "intentional lighting".

Target result:

- readable silhouette
- visible depth separation
- one clear focal subject

Rules:

- background, fog, and light colors must agree
- if fog is dark, do not bury the subject
- if the model is white, give it shape with angle light, not just more brightness

### Phase 4: Add the HTML Layer

Time: `1-2 hours`

The websites you like are not pure WebGL.
They are WebGL plus typography.

Build:

- logo top-left
- manifesto / short paragraph top-right
- scroll hint bottom-left

Keep the text outside the canvas.

Target result:

- the page reads like a brand site, not a graphics demo

### Phase 5: Add Motion

Time: `2-4 hours`

Motion order:

1. pointer-based camera drift
2. model idle motion
3. intro fade/stagger with GSAP
4. scroll-driven transitions later

Do not start with complex timelines.

Target result:

- camera drifts subtly
- scene feels alive
- nothing feels game-like or twitchy

Rules:

- keep camera easing slow
- avoid large pointer multipliers
- do not drive every object independently

### Phase 6: Add Postprocessing

Time: `1-2 hours`

Install:

`bash
npm i @react-three/postprocessing postprocessing
`

Start with:

- bloom

Maybe later:

- vignette
- noise

Avoid at first:

- large effect stacks
- heavy depth effects
- uncontrolled glow

Target result:

- highlights feel cinematic, not blurry

### Phase 7: Performance Pass

Time: `2-4 hours`

This matters early.
Fancy scenes that drop frames are not premium.

Check:

- texture sizes
- GLB size
- draw calls
- shadow settings
- mobile viewport behavior
- postprocessing cost

Rules:

- compress assets
- keep one clear hero model
- avoid unnecessary transparent surfaces
- test on a weaker laptop before calling it done

## Exact Next Steps In This Repo

Do these in order.

### Step 1

Refactor the current files:

- move canvas code out of `app/page.tsx`
- move current scene into `components/scene/hero-scene.tsx`
- move camera follow logic into `components/scene/camera-rig.tsx`
- leave `app/page.tsx` responsible only for layout

Time: `45-90 min`

### Step 2

Replace `Box` with `HeroModel`.

Create:

- `components/scene/hero-model.tsx`

Temporarily, if you do not have an asset yet:

- keep a primitive fallback
- but structure the component around future GLTF loading

Time: `30-60 min`

### Step 3

Add overlay UI.

Create:

- `components/ui/hero-overlay.tsx`

Include:

- brand mark
- one short block of copy
- scroll prompt

Time: `45-90 min`

### Step 4

Install postprocessing and add bloom.

Time: `20-30 min`

### Step 5

Bring in one GLB asset and tune:

- scale
- position
- rotation
- lighting
- fog density

Time: `2-4 hours`

### Step 6

Build version 2 of the hero from scratch after version 1 works.

This is important.
Do not just keep patching version 1 forever.

Time: `4-8 hours`

## Suggested File Structure

Use this structure next:

`txt
app/
  layout.tsx
  page.tsx
  globals.css

components/
  scene/
    hero-scene.tsx
    hero-model.tsx
    camera-rig.tsx
    scene-lights.tsx
  ui/
    hero-overlay.tsx

public/
  models/
  textures/
`

## Daily Practice Plan

If you want the fastest improvement, use this loop.

### Day 1

- refactor structure
- build clean hero canvas
- add overlay UI

Time: `2-3 hours`

### Day 2

- import one GLB
- fix scale, framing, lighting
- tune fog

Time: `2-4 hours`

### Day 3

- add bloom
- add pointer camera drift
- add intro motion

Time: `2-3 hours`

### Day 4

- rebuild the hero with a new visual direction
- compare both versions

Time: `2-4 hours`

That 4-day loop is enough to learn more than another week of isolated Three.js experiments.

## What To Learn Later

Only after the hero workflow feels normal:

- shaders
- noise fields
- particles
- scroll-driven camera paths
- scene transitions
- Blender-based custom scenes

Do not start here.

## Common Mistakes

Avoid these:

- spending too long on primitive-only demos
- mixing camera, model, and page UI logic in one file
- using black fog on a bright scene without composition intent
- overusing bloom
- importing giant assets
- building effects before layout and typography
- skipping mobile checks
- trying to imitate the exact reference before understanding the build layers

## What "Good" Looks Like

Your first good milestone is not:

- custom shader wizardry
- complex physics
- massive scene complexity

Your first good milestone is:

- one polished hero
- one imported model
- one strong overlay
- one coherent light/fog setup
- one subtle motion system
- good enough performance to ship

## Fastest Route To Taste

The learning sequence is:

1. copy one reference composition
2. rebuild it with different assets
3. rebuild it again with different lighting
4. reduce complexity
5. improve typography

Taste improves from repetition and comparison, not from reading more API docs.

## Recommended Personal Target

For the next `7 days`, aim for this:

- ship one landing hero you would put on your portfolio
- use one GLB asset
- use bloom
- use fog
- use HTML overlay
- use pointer camera drift
- keep the repo clean and typed

That is the correct next milestone for your current level.

## If You Want Me To Execute The Plan

The fastest useful implementation step in this repo is:

1. refactor the current scene into `components/scene/*`
2. add a `hero-overlay`
3. install postprocessing
4. prepare the model pipeline for a GLB asset

That will convert this project from a Three.js experiment into the right base for `igloo.inc`-style learning.
